All four claims pass in their stated supporting scope. None is a global recurrence theorem. Two minor precision improvements are noted below; no substantive defect was found.

### EXACT_BULK_CERTIFICATE_SEARCH.md

For alpha=1/p, the boundary dissipativity test becomes a polynomial sentence in nonnegative u with sum u_i^p=1 and product u_i=0. The established small-alpha result guarantees acceptance for all sufficiently large integer p. Compactness supplies a rational strictly negative margin, so reciprocal enumeration and real quantifier elimination terminate.

The exact normalized adjoint L*mu/mu is algebraic even though mu itself contains factorials: all factorial ratios have fixed integer shifts and reduce to finite products or reciprocals thereof. Positive p-th roots can be introduced as uniquely specified auxiliary variables. A rational stoichiometric affine space has rational linear defining equations. The conservation/escape proof works for real positive points as well as integer states, so the bad real semialgebraic set is bounded after choosing K. The final QE search is therefore genuinely justified and is not an implicit appeal to integer quantifier elimination.

Minor precision: explicitly reserve slack, e.g. certify H≤−4eta on the simplex boundary, use continuity to get H≤−2eta nearby, and choose the factorial error≤eta. This makes the eta-to-K-to-R order completely unambiguous. The elementary error constants can be overestimated rationally. No efficiency, manageable coefficient size, or boundary completion follows.

At (A,C,B)=(0,N,0), only immigration is outgoing, at rate one. The sole valid incoming connector is clearing from (3,N,4), with rate 6*24=144. The sigma ratio is

Each product factor is at least 1/2, and three successive normalization bounds give a fixed positive lower bound on Z_N/Z_(N+3). Hence this ratio is at least cN³. # A concrete global representation tested and falsified

The bulk/strip obstruction suggests replacing sector selection by a global residual-activity norm. Let d_y be complex outgoing rate, let s_y be a positive stationary weight for the finite embedded complex chain, and test

    nu_alpha(x)=[sum_available_y s_y^(1/alpha)/(x−y)!]^alpha,
    mu_alpha(x)=nu_alpha(x)/q(x),

where q is the actual physical total rate, and the quotient is defined on states with q>0 (as everywhere in the displayed example). The division by q automatically adds the correct inverse-activity polynomial suppression on many bounded-coordinate strata. Unlike a sector partition, the selector is everywhere positive and contains no cutoff zeros. This is an actual proposed global construction, not an assumption.

It fails, even for the deficiency-zero single-linkage cycle

    0 --1--> A+B --2-->2A+3B --3-->0.

The embedded complex chain is a directed cycle, so take s_y=1 for all three vertices (normalization is irrelevant). At x=(n,1),

    nu(x)=(n+1)^alpha/(n!)^alpha,
    q(x)=1+2n.

Incoming0→A+B from(n−1,0) contributes n^alpha/(n!)^alpha. The other possible incoming reaction is2A+3B→0 from(n+2,4). Its incoming flux equals

    (n!)^(−alpha) R_n [1+1/(6(n+1))+1/(24(n+1)(n+2))]^alpha,

where

    R_n=72(n+2)(n+1)/[72(n+2)(n+1)+8(n+2)+1]→1.

Therefore

    (n!)^alpha (L*mu_alpha)(n,1)
      =n^alpha−(n+1)^alpha

      →1

for every fixed0<alpha<1. Hence the adjoint is positive on an infinite boundary sequence. These states lie in the communicating class of0 for every n≥1. Every stated firing is enabled.

Exact phase-resolvent corrections, not merely a positive algebraic softmax of residual factorials, are needed.

# The single-linkage hypothesis in the new bulk certificate is substantive

Internal exact calculation; no recurrence counterexample.

Consider the weakly reversible network

    2A --100--> A+B --1-->2A,
    0 <--> A, 0 <--> B (all four rates1).

The first linkage conserves total population and is quadratic. The second is lower-order and gives a full-rank unbounded communicating class. For mu_alpha=(A!B!)^(−alpha), alpha∈(0,1), along A~c n,B~n the leading quadratic adjoint coefficient is

    F_alpha(c)=100 c^(2−alpha)+c^(1+alpha)−100c²−c.

F_alpha(1)=0 and F_alpha'(1)=−99alpha<0. Therefore for every fixed alpha>0 there exists c<1 sufficiently close to1 with F_alpha(c)>0. All exact factorial errors and the inflow/outflow linkage terms are lower-order than n². Hence L*mu_alpha>0 on an infinite interior ray.

Thus choosing alpha smaller does not extend the unweighted fractional-factorial bulk certificate to arbitrary multiple linkages. A fast closed linkage can create positive adjoint divergence while the genuinely confining linkage acts at lower order. This network itself is positive recurrent: the fast reaction preserves A+B and the slow network has total-population drift2−(A+B).

A fixed fugacity correction can repair this particular fast reversible linkage, so this example does not rule out a general corrected measure. Its purpose is to prevent importing the single-linkage proper-support contraction into a case where an entire fast linkage has no killing.
